summary: São Tomé and Príncipe's pledges span restoration, conservation, and agriculture. Restoration targets include assisted natural regeneration of 17,621 ha of secondary forest (≈20% of current forest cover), natural regeneration of 3,537 ha, planting of 250 ha of native species, and enrichment of 20,130 ha of shade forests and crop diversification (≈23% of forest cover), strengthening the FOLU carbon sink to -337.19 Gg CO₂eq by 2030. Conservation measures aim to cut timber use by 30%, firewood/charcoal consumption by 50%, and forest conversion to agriculture, settlements, and savanna by 15% each, while preventing savanna fires on 4,402 ha and distributing 39,600 improved stoves. Agriculture pledges include 100% organic agriculture, 2,035 ha of solar-powered irrigation (≈28% of agricultural land), 50% conservation agriculture, and 60% IPM adoption by 2035. The country also commits to restoring net carbon sink status by 2030–2035.
